note: path -> Drive file ID, so the reviewer can look files up by ID instead of by title (title search is unreliable). Written by `pnpm mirror:ids`, which requires live Drive access and is NOT run by handoff — handoff copies files by PATH into a Drive for Desktop folder and never takes an ID as input, so it cannot mis-address a write. See scripts/mirror-code.mjs for the whole mechanism.
verifiedHow: Listed the folder's live contents via the Drive connector and matched every recorded id to the title it actually resolves to. All 13 documents resolved to their expected titles; 0 mismatches, 0 missing. The census trio (deferred.md, deferred.csv, deferred.xlsx) was learned on 2026-08-17; deferred.csv was created at 16:56:34Z and updated in place at 18:28:27Z carrying the author's Disposition column, same id — the update-in-place behaviour holding for an author-edited file, not only a generated one.
idStability: VERIFIED, not assumed. Every one of the ten has a createdTime days older than its modifiedTime (CLAUDE.md created 2026-08-11T08:13:10Z, modified 2026-08-17T07:50:43Z), which is the signature of update-in-place: Drive for Desktop turns a copyFileSync overwrite into a new revision of the same file and keeps the id. Delete-and-recreate would reset createdTime on every handoff. The document mirror therefore does NOT recreate files, and the code mirror inherits the same mechanism because it writes the same way.
